conversation.content:
Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you're experiencing as a new mother, and I'm honored to be a part of your support system during this time. 

As we discuss your postpartum experience, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand how you're feeling. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common during the postpartum period. It's essential to remember that this assessment is not a diagnosis but rather a way for us to explore your emotions and concerns together.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and respected. My goal is to create a safe, supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings without judgment. I'm here to listen and provide guidance, not to criticize or assume anything about your experiences.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us understand your emotional state over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings as openly as you'd like. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll be here to support you throughout our conversation.

Let's begin with the first question. Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself, and have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do?

(sighing) Honestly, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and sad a lot of the time. It's like, I'm happy to have my baby, but at the same time, I just feel so tired and anxious all the time. I worry about my baby's health and safety constantly, and it's hard for me to shake off those thoughts. As for enjoying things I usually like to do... (pausing) I don't know, it just feels like everything is so much harder now. I used to love reading and taking walks, but lately, I just can't seem to find the energy or interest in doing those things. I mean, I'll try to read a book, but I'll just end up falling asleep after a few pages because I'm so exhausted. And even when I do try to do something I enjoy, I just feel guilty because I'm not spending that time with my baby. It's like, I'm torn between being a good mom and taking care of myself, and it's really frustrating. (looking down) I just feel like I'm not doing anything right, and that's a really hard feeling to deal with.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking head) Not as much as I used to, unfortunately. I mean, I'll have moments where I'll laugh at something my baby does, but it's not the same as it used to be. I just feel so serious and worried all the time, it's hard for me to find the humor in things like I used to. And even when I do laugh, it's not as carefree as it used to be. I'll be laughing, and then suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness or anxiety wash over me, and it's like, I don't know, it's just hard to explain. (pausing) I guess I just don't feel like myself anymore, and that's really scary for me. I feel like I've lost my sense of humor, and that's something that used to be a big part of who I am. (looking down, frowning) It's just really hard for me to find joy in things like I used to, and that's making me feel really sad and discouraged.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(sighing) Not really, to be honest. I mean, I'll think about things that are coming up, like my baby's upcoming check-up or a visit from family, and instead of feeling excited or looking forward to it, I just feel anxious. I worry about whether my baby is going to be okay, or whether I'm going to be able to get everything done that I need to do. And even when I do think about things that used to bring me joy, like going out with friends or trying a new restaurant, I just feel overwhelmed by the thought of having to take care of my baby and figure out how to make it work. (shaking head) It's like, I just feel so caught up in the day-to-day of taking care of my baby, and I'm so tired all the time, that I don't really have the energy to think about the future or look forward to things like I used to. (pausing) Sometimes I'll catch myself thinking, "What's the point of even planning anything? I'm just going to be stuck at home with the baby anyway." And that's a really sad feeling, because I used to love making plans and looking forward to things. Now it just feels like everything is so much work, and I don't have the energy or the motivation to enjoy the things I used to love.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding) Oh, yes. All the time. I feel like I'm constantly beating myself up over things that I think I'm doing wrong as a mom. If my baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If my baby is not sleeping well, I think it's because I'm not establishing a good routine. If my baby is not eating well, I think it's because I'm not making the right food choices. (sighing) It's like, I just feel so guilty all the time, like I'm not good enough, like I'm failing my baby in some way. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, if I forget to burp my baby, or if I don't get a chance to take a shower, I'll think to myself, "What kind of mom forgets to burp her baby? What kind of mom can't even take care of herself?" (shaking head) It's just this constant stream of negative self-talk, and it's really hard to turn off. (looking down) Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for someone to tell me that I'm doing everything wrong, that I'm a terrible mom. And that's a really scary feeling, because it makes me wonder if I'm really cut out for this whole mom thing.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, all the time. I mean, I'll be sitting there, just feeding my baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if she's not gaining enough weight? What if she's not developing normally? What if I'm not doing enough to stimulate her? (biting lip) And it's not just things that are related to her health, it's just... everything. I'll worry about things that might happen in the future, like what if I'm not able to protect her from harm? What if something bad happens to her? (shaking head) It's like, my mind just starts racing and I get caught up in all these worst-case scenarios. And the thing is, it's not even like I can rationalize myself out of it. I know that I'm being irrational, that I'm worrying about things that are unlikely to happen, but I just can't seem to stop myself. (sighing) It's like, I'm constantly on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's exhausting, because I'm not just worried about my baby, I'm worried about myself too. I'm worried that I'm not good enough, that I'm not doing enough, that I'm somehow failing her. (looking down) It's just this constant, nagging feeling of anxiety that I don't know how to get rid of.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, looking anxious) Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll just be sitting there, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like, my whole body just freezes up and I don't know what to do. (taking a deep breath) It's really scary, because I don't know what's triggering it. Sometimes it's when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Other times, it's when I'm out in public, and I'll just feel overwhelmed by all the people and the noise. (shaking head) It's like, my mind just goes into overdrive and I start thinking about all the worst-case scenarios. (looking down) I've even had a few times where I've been holding the baby, and I've just felt this overwhelming sense of fear that something was going to happen to her. Like, I'd be feeding her, and suddenly I'd think, "What if I drop her?" or "What if she chokes?" (shuddering) It's just this terrible, panicky feeling that I don't know how to shake. (pausing) And the worst part is, it's not just the fear itself, it's the guilt that comes with it. I feel like I'm a bad mom for feeling this way, like I'm not supposed to be scared or anxious. (looking up, tears in eyes) But the truth is, I am scared. I'm scared all the time, and I don't know how to make it stop.
Things have been getting on top of me

(sighing, nodding) Yes... that's a good way to put it. Things have been feeling really overwhelming lately. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to keep up with everything... it's just a lot. And sometimes it feels like it's all just too much for me to handle. (shaking head) I'll be in the middle of doing something, and I'll just feel like I'm drowning in responsibility. Like, I'll be trying to make breakfast, and the baby will be crying, and the phone will be ringing, and I'll just feel like I'm being pulled in a million different directions. (looking down) And then I'll start to feel guilty, because I'll think about all the things I'm not doing, all the things I'm not getting to. Like, I'll think about how I'm not spending enough time with my partner, or how I'm not keeping up with my friends, or how I'm not taking care of myself. (sighing) It's just this constant feeling of not being enough, of not being able to keep up. And it's exhausting, because I'm not just physically tired, I'm emotionally tired too. (pausing) Sometimes I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Like, I'm just trying to get through each day without losing my mind. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) And that's not how I want to be. I want to be able to enjoy this time with my baby, to be present and happy and fulfilled. But right now, it's just feeling really hard.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, looking down) Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and I think it's because I'm just so unhappy and overwhelmed all the time. I'll lie in bed at night, and my mind will just start racing with all these worries and fears. I'll think about the baby, and whether I'm doing everything right, and whether I'm a good mom. And then I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do the next day, and how I'm going to get everything done. (sighing) It's just this constant feeling of anxiety and stress, and it makes it really hard for me to relax and fall asleep.

And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll often wake up in the middle of the night and not be able to get back to sleep. I'll just lie there, staring at the ceiling, and feeling like I'm all alone with my thoughts. (shaking head) It's a really isolating feeling, and it's hard to shake.

I've also been having trouble sleeping because I'm always listening for the baby. I'll be lying in bed, and I'll think I hear her crying, so I'll get up to check on her. And even if she's not crying, I'll just stand there and watch her sleep, and worry about her. (looking down) It's like, I'm always on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. And that makes it really hard for me to get a good night's sleep.

(sighing) I'm just so tired all the time, and I don't know how to make it stop. I feel like I'm running on empty, and I don't know how to refill my tank. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) I just wish I could get a good night's sleep, and wake up feeling rested and refreshed. But right now, that just feels like a distant memory.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears welling up in eyes) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and I don't know how to shake it off. It's like, I'll be doing okay, and then something will happen, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. (sighing) It's hard to explain, but it's just this feeling of emptiness and hopelessness, like I'm not good enough, like I'm failing as a mom.

I've been feeling really overwhelmed by all the responsibilities of taking care of the baby, and I just feel like I'm not doing anything right. I'll look at other moms, and they seem so put together, so confident, and I just feel like I'm flailing. (shaking head) I feel like I'm just pretending to be a mom, like I'm just going through the motions, but I don't really know what I'm doing.

And it's not just the baby, it's everything. I feel like I've lost myself, like I'm not the same person I used to be. I used to be happy, carefree, and now I just feel like I'm trudging through each day, trying to survive. (looking down) I feel like I've lost my sense of purpose, my sense of identity. I'm just a mom now, and that's it. (sighing) It's a hard feeling to describe, but it's just this feeling of sadness and loss, like I'm grieving the person I used to be.

(looking up, tears streaming down face) I just wish I could be happy again, like I used to be. I wish I could enjoy this time with my baby, without feeling so overwhelmed and sad all the time. (sobbing) I just wish I could be a good mom, and feel confident, and feel like I'm doing everything right. But right now, that just feels like a distant dream.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears welling up in eyes) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be doing something, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of emotions wash over me, and I'll start crying. (sobbing) I've cried in the shower, I've cried while feeding the baby, I've even cried while driving in the car. It's just this overwhelming feeling of sadness and frustration, and I don't know how to make it stop.

Sometimes it's just little things that will set me off. Like, the other day, I was trying to make breakfast, and the baby was crying, and I just felt so overwhelmed. I started crying, and I couldn't stop. (shaking head) It was like, I was just standing there, crying and holding the baby, and I didn't know what to do.

Other times, it's just the big feelings of sadness and loss that will come over me. Like, I'll be thinking about my life before the baby, and how carefree I was, and how happy I was. And then I'll think about my life now, and how hard it is, and how overwhelmed I feel. (sobbing) And I'll just start crying, because it's just so hard to adjust to this new reality.

(looking down) I feel like I'm crying all the time, and it's just so exhausting. I'm tired of feeling sad, I'm tired of feeling overwhelmed. I just want to be happy again, I just want to feel like myself again. (looking up, tears streaming down face) But right now, that just feels like a distant dream.

(sighing) I guess what I'm trying to say is, I'm just really struggling right now. I'm struggling to adjust to motherhood, I'm struggling to take care of myself, and I'm struggling to find happiness. (sobbing) And it's just really hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, I'm supposed to be fulfilled. But right now, I just feel lost, and alone, and scared.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking head) No, that's not something I've thought about. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, and I've wondered how I'm going to get through this, but I've never thought about harming myself. (pausing) I think I've just felt really desperate for things to get better, for me to feel better, but I've never considered that as an option. (looking down) I don't think I could ever do that to my baby, or to my family. They need me, and I need to be here for them. (shaking head again) No, I don't think that's something I've ever considered.
